title: Grateful Dead Live at Oklahoma City Music Hall on 1972-11-14

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard stereo split captures a high‑energy 1972 show with standout performances of Bertha, Deal, China Cat Sunflower and a seamless He's Gone → Other One → Truckin transition.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers clear, upfront guitars with a pleasing stereo spread, though the early bass can be a bit distorted and track ordering is occasionally off. Musically the concert shines – the band is tight, the energy stays high throughout, and moments like Bertha, Deal, China Cat Sunflower and the He's Gone/Other One/Truckin segue are repeatedly praised.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and highlight both strong musical performance and good sound quality; only a few note minor technical glitches, leading to an overall high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo split gives crisp, upfront guitars; overall clear mix. Early Phil bass shows some distortion and a couple of reviewers mention track‑order glitches, but the audio is generally clean and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Set flows smoothly with a notable outro from He's Gone into an Other One jam that snaps back into Truckin', and the band’s interplay keeps momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar is prominent, crisp, and drives the segues (especially in the He's Gone/Other One transition).
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass sounds a bit distorted at the start but overall provides strong, pushing energy, notably urging the move to Truckin'.
band_member_comments.Bob: Balanced nicely with Jerry; his rhythm work shines during the Other One jam and he adds a humorous "Don't smoke!" line in Truckin'.
